facts.content: Patient reports four days of sore throat with evolving dry cough, runny nose, and fatigue.
facts.source_text: CC: 4 days of sore throat → evolving dry cough; runny nose; fatigue

facts.content: Patient has had odynophagia for one day that is improving.
Patient reports clear rhinorrhea with nasal congestion.
Patient has had a dry cough since yesterday.
Patient reports night sweats.
Patient had an initial fever that is now settling with paracetamol and ibuprofen.
facts.source_text: initial fever now settling w/ paracetamol + ibuprofen;

facts.content: Patient has mild dyspnea on exertion but no shortness of breath at rest.
facts.source_text: mild DOE, no SOB at rest;

facts.content: Patient denies chest pain.
Patient reports intermittent generalized headaches.
Patient reports slightly decreased appetite.
Patient reports increased fluid intake.
Patient denies nausea and vomiting.
Patient reports normal bowel and urinary habits.
Patient denies ear pain and ear discharge.
Patient denies rash.
Patient denies visual changes and photophobia.
Patient reports a sick contact at work who frequently sneezes and whose children are in kindergarten.

facts.content: Patient reports no past medical history.
Patient is taking paracetamol as needed.
Patient is taking ibuprofen as needed.
Patient has no known drug allergies.

Patient has a great-grandfather with eczema.
Patient lives alone.

facts.content: Patient drinks alcohol occasionally and socially.
Clinician assesses that the patient has a viral upper respiratory tract infection or influenza-like illness.

Assessment notes a four-day course of illness with improving sore throat, clear rhinorrhea with congestion, new dry cough, initial fever responsive to paracetamol and ibuprofen, night sweats, myalgias, headache, and mild dyspnea on exertion without chest pain.

facts.content: Patient is advised to rest, increase oral fluid intake, and stay off work for one to two days.

facts.content: The expected course of illness is seven to ten days.
